To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the retina is highly susceptible for excitotoxicity and that neuroprotective agents can be used to protect the retina from excitotoxicity.

excitotoxicity occurs in the retina due to the accumulation and activation of excitatory amino acid glutamate, and this neurotoxicity can be prevented using neuroprotective agents that modulate glutamate receptor activity.

the neuroprotective effects of several agents are mediated by multiple pathways, including inhibition of Ca2+-influx through GluR and voltage-sensitive Ca2+ channels, modulation of intracellular Ca2+ concentration, and inhibition of Ca2+/calmodulin-dependent protein kinase II (CaMKII).
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the neuroprotective mechanisms of GluR modulators in the retina.
the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms involved in the neuroprotection of the retina.
understanding the role of GluR-mediated excitotoxicity in ocular neurologic disorders, and the development of therapeutic strategies that may be used to prevent retinal damage.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
neuroprotective agents that act on GluRs, Ca2+-channels, and second messengers are promising candidates for the prevention and treatment of retinal neurodegeneration.

the retina is highly susceptible for excitotoxic neurodegenerative disorders, and therefore the development of new neuroprotective strategies is a promising approach to the treatment of ocular neuropathologies.
the regulation of excitatory amino acid transmission in the retina is a promising approach to prevent retinal degeneration in ocular neuropathy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
GluRs are the main target for the prevention of retinal degeneration in ocular neuroprotection.
neuroprotection in retinal degenerative conditions may occur by several mechanisms, and these mechanisms may be different for various neurodegenerative insults.

the neuroprotective agents that have been evaluated are effective in protecting the retina against excitotoxicity and hypoxia, and may be effective for the treatment of glaucoma and other retinal neurodegenerative disorders.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the retina is an excellent experimental model for the study of neuroprotective mechanisms and the development of therapeutic strategies against neurodegenerative ocular diseases.
excitotoxicity is a major factor that triggers neuronal degeneration in the retina and that several mechanisms are involved in neuroprotection.
excitotoxicity can be prevented by modulating GluR activity.
